description: Na₂Ge₄O₉ crystallizes in the trigonal P̅3c1 space group. Na is bonded in a 7-coordinate geometry to seven O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.47-2.88 Å. There are four inequivalent Ge sites. In the first Ge site, Ge is bonded to four O atoms to form GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent GeO₆ octahedra and corners with two GeO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 56-61°. There are a spread of Ge-O bond distances ranging from 1.76-1.81 Å. In the second Ge site, Ge is bonded to four O atoms to form GeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent GeO₆ octahedra and corners with two equivalent GeO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 63°. There are two shorter (1.79 Å) and two longer (1.82 Å) Ge-O bond lengths. In the third Ge site, Ge is bonded to six O atoms to form corner-sharing GeO₆ octahedra. There are three shorter (1.89 Å) and three longer (1.92 Å) Ge-O bond lengths. In the fourth Ge site, Ge is bonded to six equivalent O atoms to form corner-sharing GeO₆ octahedra. All Ge-O bond lengths are 1.95 Å. There are five inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Na and two Ge atoms. In the second O site, O is bonded in a trigonal planar geometry to one Na and two Ge atoms. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Na and two equivalent Ge atoms. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal planar geometry to one Na and two Ge atoms. In the fifth O site, O is bonded to two equivalent Na and two Ge atoms to form distorted corner-sharing ONa₂Ge₂ tetrahedra.
